templates.pattern: A clock is set correctly at 12:00 noon on Monday. It gains [G] seconds every minute. What will be the correct time when the clock shows [H]:00 PM on the same day?
templates.explanation: Clock gains [G] seconds per minute. In 6 hours = 360 minutes, it gains 360×[G] seconds = [360*G] seconds = [360*G/60] minutes. When clock shows 6 PM, real time = 6 PM minus [360*G/60] minutes.

templates.pattern: Two clocks are set correctly at 8:00 AM. Clock A gains [GA] minutes per hour. Clock B loses [LB] minutes per hour. How many minutes apart will they be after [N] hours?
templates.explanation: Clock A is ahead by [GA×N] minutes. Clock B is behind by [LB×N] minutes. Total gap = [GA×N] + [LB×N] = ([GA]+[LB])×[N] minutes.

templates.pattern: At what time between [H]:00 and [H1]:00 are the hands of a clock at right angles?
templates.explanation: Formula for right angle: (60H ± 15) × 2/11 minutes past H. Two positions exist in most hours. For H=3: (180+15)×2/11 = 32.7 min and (180-15)×2/11 = 30 min past 3.

templates.pattern: On what day of the week does [D] [MONTH] [Y] fall?
templates.explanation: Use Zeller's or odd-days method. Count odd days from a reference date to the given date.

templates.pattern: A faulty clock loses [L] minutes every [N] hours. If it shows correct time at 6:00 AM, what time will it show when the correct time is 6:00 PM?
templates.explanation: In 12 hours, clock loses ([L]/[N])×12 minutes. Shows 6 PM minus that many minutes.

templates.pattern: The minute hand of a clock overtakes the hour hand every [X] minutes (of correct time). How much does the clock gain or lose per day?
templates.explanation: Minute hand should overtake hour hand every 720/11 = 65.45 minutes. If it overtakes every [X] minutes: if [X] < 65.45, clock gains; if [X] > 65.45, clock loses. Daily gain/loss = (65.45-[X])/65.45 × 1440 minutes.

templates.pattern: What is the day of the week on 1st January [Y]?
templates.explanation: Starting from a known reference. 1 Jan 2020 = Wednesday. 2020 is leap: +2 days → 2021 = Friday. 2021 ordinary: +1 → 2022 = Saturday. +1 → 2023 = Sunday. +1 → 2024 = Monday. 2024 leap: +2 → 2025 = Wednesday.

templates.pattern: How many Sundays are there in [MONTH] [Y]?
templates.explanation: Find the day of 1st of the month, count how many Sundays fall in the month given its length.

templates.pattern: If [D1] [MONTH1] is [DAY1], what day is [D2] [MONTH2] of the same year?
templates.explanation: Count days between the two dates (accounting for month lengths and leap year), find mod 7, add to [DAY1].

templates.pattern: A clock shows 6:00. After how many minutes will the minute and hour hands form an angle of [A]° for the first time?
templates.explanation: At 6:00, angle = 180°. Minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on hour hand. Time = (180-[A])/5.5 minutes (for angles less than 180) or solve |180 - 5.5t| = [A].

templates.pattern: [P] tells [Q] that the day before yesterday was [DAY]. If [Q] meets [P] two days later and asks what day it is, what does [P] say?
templates.explanation: Day before yesterday was [DAY] → today = [DAY] + 2. [Q] meets [P] 2 days later = today + 2 = [DAY] + 4.

templates.pattern: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock will the hands of a clock be in a straight line but not together?
templates.explanation: Straight line but not together = 180° apart. Formula: (60H - 30) × 2/11 = (420-30)/11 × 2 = 780/11 = 5 5/11 minutes past 7. Answer: 7:05 5/11.

templates.pattern: A person was born on [D] [MONTH] [Y]. How old will he be on [D] [MONTH] [Y2]?
templates.explanation: Age = [Y2] - [Y] years (since birthday falls on same date).

templates.pattern: The angle between the hands of a clock is [A]°. The time is between [H]:00 and [H1]:00. What is the exact time?
templates.explanation: Use |30H - 5.5M| = [A]. Solve for M between [H]:00 and [H1]:00.

templates.pattern: If the [N]th day of a month is [DAY], what day is the last day of that month if the month has [DAYS] days?
templates.explanation: Last day = [DAYS]. Days from [N] to [DAYS] = [DAYS]-[N]. ([DAYS]-[N]) mod 7 added to [DAY].

templates.pattern: A and B start a job. A works every [A_DAYS] days and B works every [B_DAYS] days. If both start together on [DAY], on what day will they next work together?
templates.explanation: Next time together = LCM([A_DAYS],[B_DAYS]) days later from [DAY].

templates.pattern: A clock which gains uniformly was [M1] minutes slow at 3 PM on Tuesday and [M2] minutes fast at 3 PM on Thursday. When did it show correct time?
templates.explanation: From 3 PM Tuesday to 3 PM Thursday = 48 hours. Clock goes from -[M1] to +[M2] minutes = gains [M1]+[M2] minutes in 48 hours. Correct time was when gain = 0, i.e. [M1]/([M1]+[M2]) × 48 hours after 3 PM Tuesday = 24 hours after = 3 PM Wednesday.

templates.pattern: In [Y] years, what is the total number of odd days? (Y = [Y])
The time in a mirror image of a clock shows [H]:[M]. What is the actual time?
templates.explanation: Mirror time + actual time = 11:60 (or 12:00 for some conventions). Actual time = 11:60 - [H]:[M] (subtract minutes and hours).

templates.pattern: Two trains depart from the same station at [T1] and [T2]. Train 1 runs daily and Train 2 runs every [N] days. If both depart together on [DAY], after how many days will they depart together again?
templates.explanation: Train 1 runs every 1 day. Train 2 runs every [N] days. LCM(1,[N]) = [N] days.

templates.pattern: If a year starts on [DAY], on which day does it end (ordinary year)?
templates.explanation: Ordinary year = 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. End day = start day + 1 (since 365 mod 7 = 1).

templates.pattern: A clock gains [G] minutes per day. It is set correctly at 12:00 noon on [DAY1]. What time does it show exactly [N] days later at noon?
templates.explanation: Total gain = [G] × [N] minutes. Clock shows 12:[G×N] PM (if gain < 60 min).

templates.pattern: In which year between [Y1] and [Y2] does the calendar repeat for the first time from [Y1]?
templates.explanation: A calendar repeats after 6, 11, or 28 years depending on leap year cycles. For ordinary year 2023 (starts Sunday): same calendar in 2034 (11 years). 2024 (leap, Monday): repeats in 2052 (28 years). 2019 (Tuesday): 2030. 2020 (leap, Wed): 2048. 2021 (Friday): 2027. 2022 (Saturday): 2033.

templates.pattern: A clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock... How many times will it strike in [N] hours starting from 1 o'clock?
templates.explanation: In 12 hours, total strikes = 1+2+3+...+12 = 78. In [N] hours from 1 o'clock: sum 1 to [N] for N≤12.

templates.pattern: Ram remembers his friend's birthday is between [D1] and [D2] [MONTH]. Shyam remembers it is between [D3] and [D4] [MONTH]. On which date is the birthday?
templates.explanation: Birthday must fall in the intersection of both ranges: between max([D1],[D3]) and min([D2],[D4]) = between [D3] and [D2]. The overlapping date(s) narrow down to a single answer.
